name: Hashub
overview: The name Hashub, also rendered Hasshub, appears in the book of Nehemiah as a significant figure among the returned exiles who participated in the restoration of Jerusalem. Identified as the son of Pahath-moab and a Levite, Hashub is noted as a head of a family who actively helped repair sections of the city walls and towers, demonstrating faithful service in rebuilding the community (Nehemiah 3:11, 3:23). His lineage continued through Levites such as Shemaiah, highlighting the ongoing priestly and communal role of his family in post-exilic Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11:15).
